entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The confidence assigned to a specified proposition that one factor causally influences another.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC151; SRC109.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Guides prediction, responsibility attribution, and selection of actions believed to have leverage.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Causal Belief Strength
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = stronger belief in the specified causal relation.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The amount and organization of accurate knowledge held about a specified domain.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC151; SRC109.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Improves interpretation, prediction, option generation, and error detection within the domain.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Domain Knowledge
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often durable; accessibility and confidence can change faster than underlying knowledge.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater accurate and usable domain knowledge.
entities.representationScale: Test score; calibrated knowledge profile; concept coverage and accuracy

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The degree to which a stimulus, claim, person, or action feels previously encountered or known.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC125; SRC171.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Can increase fluency, liking, perceived truth, and default acceptance while remaining separable from recollection and accuracy.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Familiarity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often durable; accessibility and confidence can change faster than underlying knowledge.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = stronger feeling of prior exposure or knowing.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The readiness with which a specified memory, concept, or association can be retrieved under current cues.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC152; SRC125.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Increases the likelihood that retrieved content shapes appraisal, prediction, and choice.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Memory Accessibility
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = faster or more probable retrieval under the specified cue.
entities.representationScale: Low–high accessibility; response latency; recall probability

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The degree of confidence that a specified memory or recollection is accurate.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC169; SRC184.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Changes reliance on recalled information and willingness to revise or communicate it.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Memory Confidence
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater subjective confidence in memory accuracy.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The degree to which a person's internal representation of a situation forms a connected, noncontradictory account that supports inference.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC151; SRC109.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Supports prediction and planning by permitting consistent simulation of relationships and outcomes.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Mental Model Coherence
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often durable; accessibility and confidence can change faster than underlying knowledge.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = more internally coherent representation.
entities.representationScale: Low–high coherence; concept-map consistency; model-fit score

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Equating familiarity, accessibility, confidence, and accuracy, or treating a mental model as an objective system description.
entities.definition: The degree to which new information is perceived as consistent with the person's existing beliefs or expectations.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC153; SRC117.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Knowledge tests; recall/recognition tasks; concept mapping; confidence ratings; structured elicitation
entities.measurementCaveats: Accessible or familiar information may be inaccurate; observed recall depends on cues and does not fully reveal stored representation.
entities.mechanism: Changes ease of integration, scrutiny, affective response, and likelihood of belief updating.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cue match, recency, interference, expertise, motivation, stress, and context congruence.
entities.name: Prior-Belief Congruence
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually reversible as cues, resources, or interpretations change; repeated appraisal can stabilize.
entities.polarityDirection: Negative values = contradiction; positive values = congruence.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Retain dose, exposure, and baseline conditions from edge-level evidence.
relationships.generalizabilityContext: The proposed edge is causally interpretable at the stated scope. V2 implementation must preserve conditions, level transition, lag, and evidence rather than treating it as universal.
relationships.levelTransitionMechanism: The source state reaches the target unit through the exposure, communication, allocation, aggregation, or embodied-response process stated in the mechanism.
relationships.mechanism: Repeated exposure increases familiarity even when it does not establish truth.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Scope to the specified population, exposure, context, and measurement interval; test source credibility/attention where information is involved.
relationships.generalizabilityContext: The proposed edge is causally interpretable at the stated scope. V2 implementation must preserve conditions, level transition, lag, and evidence rather than treating it as universal.
relationships.levelTransitionMechanism: The source state reaches the target unit through the exposure, communication, allocation, aggregation, or embodied-response process stated in the mechanism.
relationships.mechanism: Factual veracity changes the accuracy of learned causal beliefs, conditional on exposure and acceptance.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Attribution of ease, prior exposure, expectation, and stimulus type
relationships.generalizabilityContext: Generalizability is limited to contexts compatible with the stated mechanism, conditions, and evidence.
relationships.mechanism: Ease of processing can be misattributed to prior exposure and increase subjective familiarity.
relationships.notesCaveats: Migrated from v1 relationship type: Candidate causal influence. Legacy functional form: Saturating.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Belief strength, moral conviction, accountability, involvement, and source credibility
relationships.generalizabilityContext: Generalizability is limited to contexts compatible with the stated mechanism, conditions, and evidence.
relationships.mechanism: Information that contradicts strong prior beliefs often elicits more counterarguing than congruent information.
relationships.notesCaveats: Migrated from v1 relationship type: Candidate causal influence. Legacy functional form: Threshold / asymmetric.
